minutes_text:
Arts Commission

  Inglewood, California
  January 21, 2026

A meeting of the Inglewood Arts Commission convened on January 21, 2026. Chairman
Jacques Lesure called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m., followed by the flag salute.

Ramara Rubin announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:
   Commissioner Olivia Alvitre, District No. 2
   Commissioner Anya Christiansen, District No. 4
   Chairman Jacques Lesure, Commissioner at Large
  Absent:
   Commissioner Aletha Metcalf, District No. 1
   Commissioner Phyllis Battle, District No. 3

  Council/Agency/Authority Members:
   Dionne Faulk  City Councilwoman, District No. 4

  City Personnel present were as follows:
   Kerri Arroyo  Library Director
   Ramara Rubin  Secretary

ANNOUNCEMENTS.
  a. Councilwoman Dionne Faulk, District No. 4, announced the passing of
  Commissioner Vickie Perryman-Banks. The assembly observed a moment of
  silence.

PUBLIC COMMENTS.
  a. MonaLisa Whitaker inquired regarding the relocation of public artworks and the
  contact method for artists.

MINUTES. Chairman Alvitre moved, and Commissioner Christiansen seconded, that the
minutes for the Arts Commission meeting held on October 15, 2025 be approved.
The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Alvitre, Christiansen, and Lesure
Noes: None
   Arts Commission

  DISCUSSION.
  a. Tracy Michelle introduced an art proposal to utilize vacant space for statues
  and other public art installations and requested a formal presentation next
  month to include a budget.

  VERBAL REPORTS-Public Art‐Related Projects.
  a. Rasta Asaru El provided an update on the Utility Art Box Program including
  the selection of artists and maintenance of existing boxes. The program
  covers 45 boxes in Phase I, with a total of 200 boxes.
  b. Potential Art Project (Deferred Notation – Acknowledgment of Receipt Only)
  c. Inglewood Artists Pentathlon - Artist Community Proposal for LA28 Cultural
  Olympiad (Deferred Notation - Acknowledgment of Receipt Only)
  d. Kerri Arroyo, Library Director, presented on the RFP-0259 the Crenshaw-
  Imperial Branch art installation and updates about exterior upgrades, and
  movement of public artworks; (Self Evident (for Sally Hemings) by Tori Ellison)
  from IPL to Inglewood Senior Center (temporary), art transfer (Inglewood
  Genesis by June Edmonds and Lockhaven Community Center youth) from the
  Main Library to Morningside Park Branch (permanent), art documentation
  and removal (Inglewood Stories by Michael Massenburg).
  e. Kerri Arroyo, Library Director, provided an update on the RFP-0258 Public Art
  Consultant, maintenance of The History of Transportation Mural by Helen
  Lundeberg, and the public art fund balance of $1,242,351.75

PUBLIC REMARKS.
  a. Helen Lessick announced the passing of artist Stan Smith, recommended that
  the commission consider the Cultural Olympiad proposal, and inquired about
  the process for the Crenshaw-Imperial Branch artwork installation.
  b. Joyce Dallal, inquired about the status of the Hollywood Park development’s
  artwork and the selection of Inglewood artists.
  c. Jorge Gomez announced partnership with Hollywood Park for the Inglewood
  Night Market, aiming for an early fall event.
  d. Allen Frimpong, provided an update on the feasibility study for a cultural
  district in downtown Inglewood.
  e. Melat O., introduces a community storytelling project documenting the
  histories of Inglewood residents and community members focused on
  cultural preservation.
 COMMISSIONERS’ COMMENTS/INITIATIVES/ART CALENDAR.
  a. The Arts Commissioners expressed their condolences for Vickie
  Perryman-Banks and family and welcome newly appointed
  Commissioner Anya Christiansen, District No. 4.

There being no further business to be presented, Chairman Lesure declared the meeting
adjourned at 7:32 p.m.
